stem: A clinical research study measures treatment response rate across 4 trial sites, each containing multiple patient cohorts. trial site A has 15 observations with mean 48.4 % (within-trial site SD = 4.3). trial site B has 5 observations with mean 41.4 % (within-trial site SD = 9.4). trial site C has 5 observations with mean 75.6 % (within-trial site SD = 4.5). trial site D has 15 observations with mean 59.6 % (within-trial site SD = 8.2). The between-trial site standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 7.1 and 17.7 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true treatment response rate for trial site B, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-trial site variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for trial site B: 42.9 % (shrunk from raw 41.4). Range [42.1, 45.0] as between-trial site SD varies from 7.1 to 17.7. Pooled mean: 55.1.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 55.1 % (weighted average of 4 trial site means).
Shrinkage factor for trial site B: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=11.8: B = 0.887.
Interval [42.1, 45.0] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (41.4) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (55.1) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
